answer.reason: The new array print guard cannot reject a parser-produced array solely for its depth. Parsing and both print paths start at depth zero; arrays and objects apply the same guard before incrementing depth. The unchanged harness prints only the returned parse tree. The same obligation is satisfied before and after the change.

scope_contract.reason: Printing parser-produced arrays belongs to this entry’s parse-and-print operation.

feasible_trigger.reason: No finite input can make a parser-produced array reach the new guard at a depth the parser accepted: both start at zero and apply the same limit to every array and object.

observable_consequence.reason: For the frozen condition, the added guard cannot cause the claimed depth-only print failure. The harness also contains no assertion that a print result must be nonnull.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: Natural JSON inputs already route parser-accepted arrays through the selected print call; the added guard does not block those depths in either buffered or unbuffered printing.

identity_preserved.reason: The comparison uses the same parser-produced array and the same fixed harness on both sides. The old array printer has no depth guard; the new one rejects only a depth parsing already rejects.
